$readme: A complete, valid onboarding-answers/1 example with FICTIONAL addresses. Copy it to tasks/onboard-<slug>.answers.json (or generate a template with `npm run onboard -- --address <token>`), replace every value with what you verified, and run `npm run onboard -- --address <token> --answers <file> --write`. Fields starting with $ are ignored. Every decision needs evidence: a URL or one sentence.
name: Example Token

staking.$decisions: "contracts" = you found the mechanism and verified its address (list it). "none" = you searched the project docs and the explorer and NO staking, locking or vote-escrow mechanism exists. "unresolved" = a mechanism exists but you cannot verify its address: stop; --write refuses it until the owner supplies the address or a source.
staking.evidence: https://docs.example.org/staking lists the staking contract; it holds 210M EXMP on the explorer's holder list

cex.evidence: EVM-only token: the Dune spellbook sync (sync-cex-wallets.yml) fills the exchange list nightly
cex.$rejected: Non-EVM only: wallets the runner listed after the first snapshot as labelled exchange wallets that hold the token, which you checked and refused. Each row: {"chain", "address", "note"}.

$largeHolders: One row per wallet above 1% of supply. "labelled" = the wallet is already classified (exchange, treasury, team, staking, pool) in the lists above or in config. "retail" = you traced it and it is an ordinary large holder. "unknown" = you traced it and could not establish who it is, and found no exchange, treasury or team evidence. Never guess a label: use "unknown". "retail" and "unknown" both count as holders and raise megaHolderThreshold when the wallet is above it.

largeHolders.note: Largest holder is the treasury multisig listed in wallets

copy.description: Example Token governance token (ERC-20 on Ethereum).
